Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence — follow-up + next steps

Thanks again for your time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery + the next steps we discussed. Attaching a short SLO summary and the test CSV we collected from the call demo for reference.

Summary of requirements you communicated:
- Primary SLO: time-to-first-token (TTFT) target ~120ms (median), p95 goal <200ms for interactive flows.
- Streaming mode: required for chat UX — SSE preferred, WebSocket acceptable.
- Chunk cadence: cadence target roughly 80–120ms between chunks for a smooth UX (ideally no >200ms gaps).
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 50 concurrent streaming sessions, scale to 200 concurrent during peak. Peak QPS ~200; average response ~300–400 tokens.
- Failure mode: graceful degradation to a smaller model (lower-cost variant) if latency exceeds threshold.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) We will run a Redwood perf lab with a workload that mirrors your average response length (350 tokens) and streaming cadence. (Owner: Redwood — Rishi & Vivek).
2) Please confirm the expected peak concurrency and if you have an internal perf script we should use. If not, we can use the attached CSV request traces as a seed.
3) Schedule technical deep-dive: propose Wed 2027-04-07 10:00 PT. Please confirm availability.

Attachments: acme_slo_summary.pdf, ttft_latency_test_results.csv

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that captures it well. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Concurrency: 50 concurrent streams is the baseline; our internal SLA requires handling bursts up to ~200 concurrent streams (short windows, 2–5 minutes).
- Throughput: peak QPS 180–220; typical QPS 40–70. Avg tokens per streaming response is ~350.
- Transport: SSE is our preferred integration (server-sent events) because our front-end infra handles SSE natively; WebSocket is acceptable as fallback.

Questions for the perf run:
1) Can Redwood simulate our burst profile (50 → 200 over 60s) and report median/p95 TTFT and chunk cadence distribution?
2) Do you have an SDK or sample perf script we can run on our side?
3) What's the expected TTFT delta if we enable prefix caching for repeated prompts?

If you can also share recommended model variants and quantization profiles for this workload that would help our procurement evaluation.

Sam

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence — follow-up + next steps (perf plan)

Thanks for the context — quick technical note and proposed lab configuration. I’ll own the perf run with Vivek.

High-level plan:
- Lab objective: validate TTFT SLOs (median 120ms, p95 <200ms) under target concurrency and burst profiles, and characterize chunk cadence for SSE.

Test config (initial):
- Model: open-llama-like (recipe) / production candidate — we’ll test both the 7B quantized and a higher-capacity 13B float variant to measure tradeoffs.
- Quantization: int8/4-bit profiles as available — measure TTFT impact.
- Instance type: dedicated GPU nodes (A100), with a small pool to simulate warm KV cache and cold starts.
- Workload: avg response 350 tokens, chunk policy = streaming output with chunk flush every ~50–150ms simulated latency.
- Concurrency: baseline 50 concurrent streams, burst to 200 over 60s windows.

Metrics to collect: median/p50 TTFT, p95/p99 TTFT, end-to-end response latency, chunk cadence histogram (ms between chunks), tokens/sec per-session, CPU/GPU utilization, and observed batching sizes.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Median TTFT <= 120ms on warm instances with target concurrency.
- p95 TTFT <200ms.
- Chunk cadence: 75–125ms median inter-chunk gap; <5% gaps >250ms.

Deliverables:
1) Perf script (we’ll provide a Docker image + load generator) — will post link to internal drive.
2) Raw CSV with request traces (we’ll attach summarized results).
3) Recommendations: model variant, batching, caching, and a suggested rolling rollout plan (canary sizes).

Questions for Acme (please reply inline):
- Do you have a strict p99 TTFT requirement? If so, what is the acceptable threshold?
- Are there client-side constraints (mobile vs desktop) that affect preferred chunk cadence?

Next steps:
- I’ll spin up the lab today and run the baseline warm-run for the 7B quantized profile. Expect results and the perf script link by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule deep-dive on Wed 2027-04-07 10:00 PT (tentative).

Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
